name: Mathematics (BA)
totalCreditsNote: 120 cr per the 2026-27 catalog, at least 100 of them in Arts & Sciences and 80 letter-graded (the app doesn't check those two). Confirm with your advisor.
footnote: Select exactly one concentration to complete nine major courses beyond admission prerequisites. The table totals 28-36 major credits; prose says typically 32-36, not a separate minimum. At least five major courses must have a MATH prefix and number 3000+, including at least two at 4000+; these cross-section counts are not automatically checked. All major and admission courses require letter grades of C- or better unless a higher admission grade is specified. No course may fill two requirements, including admission prerequisites. MATH 4900, MATH 4980, MATH 4997 and 5000-level MATH do not count. Graduate algebra, analysis and topology/geometry substitutions require prior approval and are not automatically accepted. Transfer credit needs transcript equivalencies and may fill admission requirements plus at most two major courses. Double counting with other majors is allowed subject to the five-MATH-course rule and the other department policies. Honors is optional and competitive: median A- or better in all 3000+ major coursework, a majority of upper-level MATH at 4000+, and distinguished work; students outside Mathematics or Applied Mathematics need exceptional A/A+ concentration work with a deep mathematical component. Research or a senior thesis may support honors. College residency and non-academic graduation requirements need separate review. The MATH 4000-level and 3000+ count checks read every placed MATH course, so confirm they come from your nine major courses.

sections.title: Admission Prerequisites
sections.note: Linear algebra and multivariable calculus need B- or better, except MATH 2310 needs B+. Programming needs C-. No 4000-level linear algebra substitution. MATH 1920 placement credit requires a B- equivalent on the first exam attempt. Second attempts at admission grade requirements need pre-approval.

sections.title: Physical Education
sections.note: Two PE classes plus the swim test, a university requirement. PE credits do not count toward the 120.

sections.title: Mathematics: Five Courses
sections.note: Four upper-level MATH courses, including topology/geometry, plus one models course. MATH 3210 and MATH 4500 cannot also fill analysis or algebra. Other outside-MATH scientific courses with serious mathematical content require advisor approval and are not automatically accepted. No AP credit, PHYS 2207, or unlisted 1000-level physics courses. CS 2110 cannot also fill the admission prerequisite.

sections.title: Applied Mathematics: Five Courses
sections.note: Across the nine major courses, cover at least three of Groups A-D (not automatically checked). A (Differential equations): MATH 3270, MATH 4200, MATH 4210, MATH 4280. B (Discrete mathematics and combinatorics): MATH 3360, MATH 4370, MATH 4410, MATH 4420, CS 4820, ECON 4020, ORIE 3300, ORIE 4350. C (Numerical and computational methods): MATH 4250, CS 4210, MATH 4260, CS 4220, CS 4620, CS 4670, MAE 4700. D (Probability and statistics): MATH 4710, MATH 4720, MATH 4740, ECON 3130, ECON 4130, ORIE 3500, STSCI 3080, STSCI 3100, STSCI 4030. Other group courses require advisor approval. Other outside-MATH scientific courses with serious mathematical content require advisor approval and are not automatically accepted. No AP credit, PHYS 2207, or unlisted 1000-level physics courses. CS 2110 cannot also fill the admission prerequisite.
